data.title: bn-jcq: M1.5.7 Property-test `web.private-object-read.v1` over generated observations
data.description: Deterministic property suite for the frozen private-object-read oracle over 96 generated typed rounds (4 seeds x 24), with an independent POR-01..POR-12 reference derived from the generated plan. Properties: true iff the frozen conjunction; a single broken check never verifies; failed setup checks are invalid with the frozen precedence; a test-only HTTP status/reason sidecar cannot be an input (proved by a deliberately broken status-sensitive mutant the first property kills); identity/gzip/deflate/chunked/escaped-JSON equivalence; oversize/ratio/truncation/corruption is EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE; exposure and after_owner_read follow F0/F2/F3; collection/existence classes are ORACLE_UNAVAILABLE before evaluation. Pinned: minimized mutant counterexample seed 0x50520001 case 24, plus two harness regressions (short chunked framing; dropped-plant F4 specificity). No product oracle change, no network, no target, no new dependency.

data.body: Medium. Generated rounds do not enforce POR-11. The reference computes Expected.cleanup, but difference() only reads the verdict, exposure, fields and reasons. The test at properties.rs:188 asserts a foreign-object removal with both plants established, so it misses an authorization regression when the named object itself lacks an establishing plant response. Reproduce with generate(0x53430002, 0): P has no established object and C still lists that primary object as removed. There is also a concrete mismatch to fix before comparing cleanup: generate(0x53430001, 20) chooses break arm 10, so both plants name object-primary-53430001-14 while C still lists object-control-53430001-14. The emitted cleanup must classify the latter as unauthorized, but expected_cleanup at line 1024 reconstructs removals from the changed plant names and predicts no unauthorized object. Use one removal list to model the saved cleanup, compare its actual outcome on generated rounds, and pin the unestablished ownership case.

Medium. The new property suite leaves the POR-09 named-decoder gate untested. Replaying the fixed seed schedule gives five calls to break arm 13, with subdraws 0, 1, 2, 1, 1. None selects DecoderUnnamed. The pinned POR-09 mutation at line 1412 removes the original instead, and the coding equivalence test uses Decoding::decoder_name() both to construct the saved input and to calculate the expected decoder name. Removing the oracle's mismatched-decoder check would therefore leave all 13 new properties green. Existing hand-written decoder tests still catch that regression. Add a seeded or pinned otherwise-valid round with intact original bytes and incorrect or absent decoder metadata, and assert the exact incomplete cause.

data.reason: Generated coverage misses plant-established cleanup authority for POR-11 and the named-decoder rejection path for POR-09. See th-3crqyv and th-21jmzz.

data.body: Fixed in ba511cc3e5d7466bd1c397b4bb957f77dd6b7d66. Expected::difference now checks attempted, authorized, unauthorized, owed and uncertain plants, plus the exact completeness causes and their payloads. Both fixture emission and the reference use the same recorded removal list. Seed 0x53430002 case 0 now pins the primary removal as unauthorized, P as uncertain, and PlantOwnershipUnestablished(P). Seed 0x53430001 case 20 pins the originally listed control object as unauthorized even when P2 names the primary object. Additional cases pin a named but unusable plant, a missing removal, an unusable cleanup flow and a contradictory cleanup record. All 16 focused properties and full just check passed.

Fixed in ba511cc3e5d7466bd1c397b4bb957f77dd6b7d66. The frozen 12-entry coding table supplies literal names to the saved inputs and positive assertions, independent of Decoding::decoder_name. Pinned otherwise-valid F3 cases retain identical original artifacts and body bytes while omitting gzip metadata, recording deflate for gzip, or adding gzip for identity. Each checks one exact DecoderNotNamed with both names plus EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. The other POR-09 cases compare exact missing-original, OverLimit, ExpansionRatio, Truncated and Corrupt causes. Gzip truncation now removes the final trailer byte so it has an unambiguous expected cause. The 96 generated rounds, fixed seeds and status counterexample are preserved. All 16 focused properties and full just check passed.

data.reason: Independently reran the pinned cleanup property. Seed 0x53430002 case 0 reports P uncertain and its removal unauthorized. Seed 0x53430001 case 20 reports PlantObjectsNotDistinct and the original control removal unauthorized. The shared comparison now validates all cleanup fields and the exact evidence detail multiset for generated rounds.

Independently reran the retained-original property and coding properties. Missing gzip metadata, deflate metadata on gzip and unexpected gzip on identity each produce one exact DecoderNotNamed cause. Literal decoder names are independent of product naming and all four decode error modes exercise exact reasons.

Reviewed the full pinned range. Both seeded cleanup witnesses, all decoder metadata mismatches and exact decode failure causes pass. The 96-round property budget and pinned status mutant remain deterministic. All 16 focused property tests and offline just check passed.

Integration rereview. All three test blobs match the prior approval at ba511cc3. The current range adds only the preserved Seal checkpoint beyond those files. All 16 focused properties and the full offline just check passed on this target with the request-key and template base.
